Pulse for 16 October 2026

The stories from 16 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

ChatGPT splits up big tasks

ChatGPT can now work like a small team: in its top paid version, several AI agents, helpers that work through a task on their own, tackle different parts of one job at the same time.

Everyday tool

ChatGPT builds your slides

ChatGPT Slides is a new ChatGPT feature that turns a chat, your notes or files into an editable slide deck you can fix together with teammates and export to PowerPoint.

New model

AI zooms in like you do

Glimpse is a new AI model from the startup Elorian that keeps going back to a picture or video while it thinks, zooming into details the way you would pinch to zoom on a phone photo.

Study

AI cracks a crypto mystery

The NIST elliptic curves are a set of shared mathematical settings that protect much of the internet's encryption, and Anthropic says a Claude research model finally explained where their mysterious starting numbers came from.

Device

Run AI agents on a laptop

A local AI PC is a laptop or desktop that runs large models on its own chips instead of sending every prompt to the cloud, and NVIDIA's new RTX Spark Windows laptops are built for that job.

New model

Host a coding AI yourself

An open-weight model is a model you can download and run yourself, and Reflection's new Beam is a 501-billion-parameter coding model released under Apache 2.0 so teams can host or customize it.
